command:
set -eo pipefail
cd /tmp
echo "== fastp on the complete SRR062634 run: the same reads bwa aligns, 3.6 GiB compressed =="
df -m /tmp | awk 'NR==2{print "tmpfs_total_mb "$2}'
# fastp streams, but input + output both live in tmpfs on this path. Sample the high-water mark.
( MAX=0; while :; do U=$(df -m /tmp | awk 'NR==2{print $3}')
    [ "$U" -gt "$MAX" ] && { MAX=$U; echo "$MAX" > /tmp/.peak; }; sleep 2; done ) & SAMPLER=$!

# Record the input digests: the pin tier for these is a RODA path, so publishing the hashes is
# what lets anyone else check they got the same bytes.
SHA1=$(sha256sum SRR062634_1.filt.fastq.gz | cut -d" " -f1)
SHA2=$(sha256sum SRR062634_2.filt.fastq.gz | cut -d" " -f1)

T0=$(date +%s)
fastp -i SRR062634_1.filt.fastq.gz -I SRR062634_2.filt.fastq.gz \
      -o out_1.fq.gz -O out_2.fq.gz -j fastp.json -h fastp.html -w 8 2> fastp.log
T1=$(date +%s); WALL=$(( T1 - T0 ))
kill "$SAMPLER" 2>/dev/null || true
PEAK=$(cat /tmp/.peak 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
# Do NOT rm the staged reads: /tmp is sticky and stage-in ran as the instance user, so the
# container gets EPERM, which `rm -f` does not suppress and which would kill the task.

# No python3 and no jq in this image -- parse with grep/awk. The FIRST total_reads in the JSON is
# summary.before_filtering; the second is after_filtering, so `head -1` is load-bearing.
getnum() { grep -oE "\"$1\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*[0-9]+" fastp.json | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+$'; }
BEFORE=$(getnum total_reads)
PASSED=$(getnum passed_filter_reads)
LOWQ=$(getnum low_quality_reads)
MANYN=$(getnum too_many_N_reads)
SHORT=$(getnum too_short_reads)
LONG=$(getnum too_long_reads)
# These are read counts in the tens of millions and bases in the billions: awk's %d is int32 and
# would clamp at 2147483647, so every derived number is printed with %.0f.
ACCOUNTED=$(awk -v p="$PASSED" -v l="$LOWQ" -v n="$MANYN" -v s="$SHORT" -v g="$LONG" \
  'BEGIN{printf "%.0f", p+l+n+s+g}')
BASES=$(getnum total_bases)
DUP=$(grep -oE '"rate"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*[0-9.eE+-]+' fastp.json | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9.eE+-]+$')
Q30=$(grep -oE '"q30_rate"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*[0-9.eE+-]+' fastp.json | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9.eE+-]+$')

# Counting the outputs is what turns fastp's own report into a claim about the files it wrote.
# `wc -l` on a decompressed stream reads to EOF, so no SIGPIPE under pipefail.
OUT1=$(awk -v n="$(gzip -dc out_1.fq.gz | wc -l)" 'BEGIN{printf "%.0f", n/4}')
OUT2=$(awk -v n="$(gzip -dc out_2.fq.gz | wc -l)" 'BEGIN{printf "%.0f", n/4}')
OUTSUM=$(awk -v a="$OUT1" -v b="$OUT2" 'BEGIN{printf "%.0f", a+b}')

{
  echo "reads_before        $BEFORE   want exactly 48297986"
  echo "                               == bwa's primary records (48817006 total - 519020 suppl.)"
  echo "total_bases         $BASES"
  echo "passed_filter       $PASSED"
  echo "low_quality         $LOWQ"
  echo "too_many_N          $MANYN"
  echo "too_short           $SHORT"
  echo "too_long            $LONG"
  echo "accounted_for       $ACCOUNTED   want == reads_before   [CONSERVATION]"
  echo "out1_reads          $OUT1"
  echo "out2_reads          $OUT2   want == out1 (mates stay paired)"
  echo "out1+out2           $OUTSUM   want == passed_filter"
  echo "q30_rate            $Q30   (observation)"
  echo "fastp_dup_rate      $DUP   (observation; sequence-based, not picard's 0.008684 by position)"
  echo "wall_s              $WALL"
  echo "tmpfs_peak_used_mb  $PEAK   <- input + output both live in RAM on this path"
  echo "sha256_R1           $SHA1"
  echo "sha256_R2           $SHA2"
} > smoke-check.txt
cat smoke-check.txt
test "$BEFORE"    -eq 48297986
test "$ACCOUNTED" -eq "$BEFORE"
test "$OUT1"      -eq "$OUT2"
test "$OUTSUM"    -eq "$PASSED"
echo "SMOKE CHECK PASSED"
